metadata.title: The Survey of Adult Skills: Reader’s Companion, Second Edition

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Reader’s Companion describes the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) design and its relationship to other skills assessments (including PISA), rather than reporting a student-level predictive analysis with an explicit analytic sample. The document explains how proficiency levels and descriptors are defined (e.g., response probability thresholds) and how scales differ across surveys, but it does not provide a modeling section specifying which survey weights were applied in an empirical ML/statistical estimation. For analysts using PIAAC microdata, the sampling design is complex and weights are typically required for population-representative estimates; however, this chapter does not specify the exact weight variables or replicate-weight procedures. Therefore, no weight variable name or replicate method can be extracted from the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The provided text is a methodological/relationship companion describing constructs, scale definitions, and comparisons between PIAAC and PISA (e.g., literacy/numeracy/proficiency level descriptors and response probability thresholds). It does not report an empirical model predicting a PV-based cognitive outcome, nor does it document any PV generation/combining or missing-data handling strategy for an analysis. As a result, plausible-value handling and missing-data handling are not applicable to the excerpt’s purpose, and missing-data handling is not reported because no estimation procedure is presented.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in the provided excerpt because the text is a companion describing the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) and its conceptual/measurement relationships to PISA and other skills surveys. The document includes annexes listing participating countries and project participants, but it does not specify inclusion/exclusion criteria for an estimation sample (e.g., grade bands, task/module completion, or missing-data exclusions).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Reader’s Companion (Second Edition) explains how the Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC) relates to other international skills assessments, especially PISA, focusing on conceptual alignment and differences in measurement. It describes how PIAAC directly assesses adult literacy/reading, numeracy/mathematical literacy, and problem solving in technology-rich environments, and it contrasts these with PISA’s target population (adults vs. 15-year-old students) and domain definitions. The excerpt also details how proficiency levels are located using response probability thresholds (e.g., RP67 vs RP80) and how this affects the interpretation of “proficiency” descriptors, while noting that estimation precision is not affected by the RP choice. It further provides comparison tables (e.g., for problem solving) and cautions against direct score comparisons across surveys without linking studies. No predictive modeling, performance metrics, or causal claims are evaluated in the provided text.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The excerpt is not an empirical ML study; it is a methodological/relationship companion that discusses assessment frameworks, construct definitions, and how proficiency descriptors are defined across surveys. Consequently, there is no student-level analytic sample, no reported predictive target variable, and no ML algorithm evaluation to extract. Sparse fields (e.g., total_students, per-country n_students, PV/missing-data handling) are absent by design because the text does not present an estimation procedure or results table for a statistical model.
